samples.question: The picture shows eighteen small round dots on a plain background. Every dot has exactly the same size and the same round shape, and no two dots touch or overlap. Fourteen of the dots are grey and four are coloured: one red, one green, one blue and one orange. Imagine stretching a rubber band around the whole group of dots and letting it snap tight, so that it forms one closed outline that encloses every one of the eighteen dots and never bends inwards. The tightened band runs straight from dot to dot and comes to rest touching only a few of them: a dot that the band touches is a corner of that outline, and every other dot lies strictly inside the outline. All eighteen dots count when the band is tightened, grey ones exactly as much as coloured ones. Exactly one of the four coloured dots is a corner of the tightened band, and the other three coloured dots lie strictly inside it. Distance from the middle of the picture does not decide the answer: a dot near the edge of the picture can still lie well inside the band, and the coloured corner dot can be closer to the middle of the picture than a coloured dot that is not a corner. The colours themselves, the dot size, the number of dots, the amount of ink and where the group sits on the page carry no information about the answer. Which coloured dot is a corner of the tightened rubber band? Answer red, green, blue or orange.
